name: run-timeline
title: Run timeline
purpose: The stations a run passes through, in order, each with its state in words: done with how long it took, running with the time so far, waiting on the owner, failed or not started.
whenToUse: At the top of a run's screen, to show which station the run is at and how the earlier ones went.
For any job that passes through three to six named stages, where the reader wants the state and the time of each.
whenNotToUse: For the steps of a form the reader fills in. Use a stepper, whose completed steps are links back.
For events in the order they happened, with who acted. Use a timeline.
For the status of a run as one row of a list. Use run status.
For the tool calls of a run. They are rows and step groups in the transcript.
For more than six stations. Group them, or show the current one in words in the page header.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: Below 768px the stations run down the page, one line each, with the state at the end of the line. At 768px and up they run across it, joined by lines, with the state under the name.

accessibility: Use an ol with the class ds-run-timeline and an aria-label that names the run. Each station is an li with ds-run-timeline__station. A screen reader announces the count and each station's place.

The app sets data-state on each li: done, running, waiting, failed or not-started. The stylesheet draws a mark of its own shape for each, and nothing else decides how a station looks. not-started, running, waiting and failed take the icon and tone of Queued, Working, Needs input and Check failed in the badge's status set.
Set aria-current="step" on the li of the station the run is at, whatever its state: running, waiting or failed. A run that has not started, or has passed its last station, has none.
ds-run-timeline__name holds the name of the station. The names are the app's own: Plan, Build, Verify, Review and Decide are only an example.

ds-run-timeline__status holds the state in words, written by the app, with a time where there is one: Done · 1 min 4 s, Running · 4 min 12 s, Waiting on you, Failed · 2 min 10 s, Not started. The mark and the colour only add to those words.
Put the time in a span with ds-run-timeline__time, or give the ds-elapsed element that class, so a narrow station wraps its status before the time and never inside it.

A time that counts up is not announced: use the ds-elapsed element from behaviors/elapsed.js, or a span with aria-live="off". The timeline is not a live region. The view's one status region says when the run moves on.
Only the running mark moves, and under prefers-reduced-motion it is still.
It holds no control and takes no focus. The component needs no script.
